name: Lake Elune'ara
summary: At Moonglade's heart, Lake Elune'ara rests beneath moonlit groves. The sacred waters honor Elune, and the Cenarion Circle's shrine grounds border its shores.

sections.title: Heart of the Sacred Vale
sections.body: Moonlit groves frame Lake Elune'ara, whose waters are said to bear the White Lady's blessing. Nighthaven lies to the north, and the Cenarion Circle's shrine grounds border the lake. Initiates have long searched its depths for lost relics. Through contact with nature's currents, they seek harmony with the land.

sections.title: The Slumber of Omen
sections.body: Ancient peril sleeps beneath Lake Elune'ara's quiet surface. Legends tell of Omen, a two-headed wolf demigod and revered ancient corrupted by the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Defeated long ago, Omen was cast into the lake bed. There he sleeps beneath the dark water, a reminder of nature's wounds.

faq.answer: Night elves and druids revere Lake Elune'ara's sacred waters at the heart of Moonglade. Its name honors the Moon Goddess Elune, and the Cenarion Circle's sanctuaries surround it.

faq.q: What lurks at the bottom of the lake?
faq.answer: Omen, a fallen demigod, sleeps in the lake's dark depths. Once a noble ancient, he was driven mad by the Burning Legion during the ancient war and cast into the lake after his defeat.

faq.q: Why do druids come to this lake?
faq.answer: Druids come to the lake for trials and to commune with the spirits of nature. Young druids search its waters for sacred relics as part of their rites of passage.

angles.text: As a druid, you know Lake Elune'ara as a place for rituals and trials. Sacred relics in its deep waters aid initiates on their path.
As a night elf, you know Lake Elune'ara by its name, which honors Elune. The lake is a place of divine peace and recalls the War of the Ancients.
